title: Polarity Inverter
pages: Craft the Polarity Inverter with iron, copper, one cobalt ingot (forge:ingots/cobalt), Purified Salts, one Rectified Filament from the Flux Rectifier and one Germanium Point-Contact Rectifier. The rectifier is the inverter's one-way current valve: saw a germanium ingot (forge:ingots/germanium) into two Germanium Wafers in the Sawmill, craft a wafer between a copper ingot (the contact whisker) above and a Porcelain Insulator below into a Rectifier Diode Blank, then feed the blank to the formed Flux Rectifier, whose current pulse electrically forms the contact into a working rectifier. A Rectified Filament or plain redstone cannot stand in for it. Its Stator Coil output unlocks the Degauss Coil before the Electrolyzer.

Place a lodestone directly beneath it, an end rod directly above it, crying obsidian on all four horizontal sides, and amethyst blocks in the four corners of the same horizontal ring. The amethyst corners brace the opposed field poles. Any missing or swapped corner, side, cap or base stops operation. Right-click the formed controller with feedstock from a loaded polarity_inversion recipe. It loads one recipe batch into its stock buffer, processes it over 40 ticks, and holds the output for empty-hand collection or bottom-face extraction. It needs no FE; hand use and the automation buffer below share the same recipes.

It runs 20 exclusive datapack polarity_inversion recipes. Nineteen invert the polarity of ranged-weapon, mount and exploration gear (bow, crossbow, trident, shield, elytra, fishing rod, flint and steel, carrot on a stick, warped fungus on a stick, lead, saddle, turtle helmet, iron/golden/diamond horse armor, name tag, map, firework rocket and spectral arrow) back into base materials at a lossy ratio, recycling scrap without a smithing table or anvil; the carrot and warped-fungus rods give back their bait and flint and steel gives back its flint. The twentieth fuses two Rectified Filaments from the Flux Rectifier into a Stator Coil.

The Stator Coil is reserved as the gate material for the next apparatus. With JEI installed, look up Polarity Inversion or inspect the Polarity Inverter catalyst to see all 20 loaded datapack recipes, input batch counts, results and formation requirements.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded polarity inversion recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch every 40 ticks (2 seconds) without power, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
